regulatory_descriptor: A Unit-linked Non-Participating Individual Life Savings Insurance Plan
variants: Gold (one of the variants of Bajaj Life Supreme)
key_benefits: Maturity Benefit — Fund Value payable on maturity (provided Life Assured is alive); option to take as lump sum or systematic payout over a maximum of 5 years (Settlement Option)
Death Benefit — higher of Prevailing Sum Assured (incl. top-up), Fund Value on date of intimation of death, or Guaranteed Death Benefit (105% of Total Premiums Paid)
Loyalty Additions — from the 16th policy year, 0.25% of average fund value of last 3 years added annually
Return of Mortality Charge (ROMC) — life-cover charges added back (100% at end of 15th year and every 5th year thereafter; 100% at maturity)
Systematic Partial Withdrawals (available after the 5-year lock-in)

eligibility.policy_term: Whole Life option available (illustration uses Whole Life with 10-year PPT); full PT range not captured in this parse
eligibility.premium_payment_term: Single / Limited / Regular (illustration uses 10-year limited pay); full range not captured in this parse
eligibility.note: Eligibility boundary table not recovered from this leaflet parse — verify against policy document. 'Gold' is one variant of the Bajaj Life Supreme plan.

key_terms.free_look_note: Free-look period not explicitly captured in this leaflet parse; standard 30 days expected for a ULIP — verify against policy document.
key_terms.grace_period: Not explicitly captured in this leaflet parse — verify against policy document.
key_terms.suicide_clause: Not explicitly captured in this leaflet parse — verify against policy document.
key_terms.lock_in_note: Unit-Linked products offer NO liquidity during the first 5 years — no full or partial surrender/withdrawal permitted until the end of the fifth year.
key_terms.tax_note: 'Tax-free fund switching' / tax benefits per prevailing Section 11 (read with Schedule II) of the Income Tax Act — subject to change; consult a tax advisor. Returns shown at 4% and 8% are illustrative and not guaranteed.

mandatory_disclosures_present: ULIP market-risk statement ('ULIPs are different from traditional insurance products and are subject to risk factors; premium is subject to investment risks; NAV may go up or down; insured is responsible for his/her decisions')
Risk Factors & Warning Statements (product name does not indicate quality/future prospects/returns)

claims_marketing_must_support: Any 'guaranteed' wording (Guaranteed Death Benefit = 105% of Total Premiums Paid, Return of Mortality Charge) is condition-bound: ROMC and Loyalty Additions do NOT apply if the policy is surrendered, discontinued or paid-up.
'Market linked returns' must be presented as 'potentially' market-linked (as the leaflet does) — not as assured.
Loyalty Additions begin only from the 16th policy year; Systematic Partial Withdrawals are available only after the 5-year lock-in.
'Tax-free fund switching' is bounded by prevailing tax law (Section 11 / Schedule II) and must carry the consult-a-tax-advisor caveat.
claims_marketing_must_avoid: Do NOT advertise 'guaranteed returns' or 'assured growth' — the fund value is subject to investment/market risk borne entirely by the policyholder; NAV may go up or down.
Do NOT show only the 8% (or any single) illustrative return as if promised — both 4% and 8% must be shown as illustrative, not guaranteed, and not as upper/lower limits.
Do NOT use the word 'tax-free' unconditionally — it must reference the prevailing Income Tax Act provisions and the consult-your-tax-advisor caveat.
Do NOT imply liquidity in the first 5 years — there is a mandatory 5-year lock-in.
Do NOT position as a pure savings/guaranteed-return instrument; it is a market-linked ULIP.
must_state: Plan UIN 116L211V02 (shared across Bajaj Life Supreme variants)

Mandatory ULIP market-risk disclosure (premium subject to investment risk; NAV may go up or down; policyholder bears the risk)
5-year lock-in / no-liquidity statement for the first five years
Standard disclaimer to read the sales brochure and policy document before concluding a sale
